description: Single source of truth for Oddtoe design values. Every other file (colors.css, typography.css, tailwind.preset.js, PowerPoint themes, video LUTs) is derived from this file. As of 1.0.0 the color palette is locked to real values — no placeholders remain. 1.1.0 adds the headline-lockup divider variants (solid + dashed) and the three lockup gap tokens. 1.2.0 narrows body widths to editorial reading rhythm (single-column 450px / two-column 840px container with 32px gap). 1.3.0 adds imagery patterns: radius.media (10px) as the system-wide image corner; carousel block (general pattern with three cell variants); image-array component-scoped sizes for the title-above-image work tile. 1.4.0 names the canonical motion engines per surface (web = GSAP + ScrollTrigger, video = After Effects → Lottie [pipeline pending], presentations = native PowerPoint transitions) and adds two new locked scroll recipes (fade-on-scroll, parallax-scroll) with the prefers-reduced-motion guard baked in. 1.7.0 adds the plaster orientation mode (paper-light ground carrying the AE texture stack) for Oddtoe's own textured social posts, with its two scoped exceptions: square-cornered hero media and a permitted cool grade.

orientation.description: Oddtoe surfaces default to color.brand.paper (#262B2A) as the canonical body background. Light-mode surfaces (color.brand.paper-light, color.ui.white-surface) are supported as a documented exception — see modes below.

marquee.use: Decks, landing pages, video, ads, hero surfaces, and any social post that is not part of the textured post family. The brand-visible default. Locked 1.6.0; social narrowed 1.7.0 when plaster landed.

longform.use: Workbooks, white papers, reports of 10+ pages, print-intended PDFs, hand-markup artifacts. Flips to paper-light with paper-dark text to solve reading fatigue, toner cost, and pen markup. Locked 1.6.0 — see 08_decisions/2026-05-12-dark-first-exception-for-longform.md.

plaster.use: Oddtoe's own textured social posts — the After Effects post family built on the plaster/ink treatment (New Growth Instagram and its siblings). Shares longform's ground and foreground, but is a separate mode because it carries the texture stack and two scoped exceptions, and because narrowing longform to cover feed posts would misread a mode written for 10-page reports. Locked 1.7.0 — see 08_decisions/2026-09-14-plaster-mode-for-textured-social.md.

exceptions.media-radius: Hero media in this mode is square-cornered, overriding radius.media (10px). The ink matte that reveals the image needs a hard edge to read as a window cut in the plaster; a 10px corner reads as a UI card sitting on top of it.
exceptions.image-grade: Hero media in this mode may be desaturated and graded cool toward color.accent.blue-muted, overriding the 'slight warmth only' rule in 02_visual-identity/imagery-style.md. The cool plate is what separates the image from the warm ground.

plaster.scope: Both exceptions are scoped to this mode only. Media anywhere else in the system keeps radius.media and the warmth rule.

primary.description: Olive-sage. Primary CTA + dominant brand surface. Every primary CTA on oddtoe.com uses this.

secondary.description: Dark olive. Hover/pressed partner to primary. Also a section-overlay tint.

paper.description: Canonical body surface (dark-first). Doubles as ink on light surfaces — see color.role.ink-on-light.

ink.description: Default type/labels on dark surfaces (paper, secondary, muted-surface, surface-warm).

paper-light.description: Warm off-white. Light-mode body surface, inverted cards, print contexts.

cream.description: Subtitle / meta text accent on dark surfaces. The Arvo subtitle line beneath a Bebas headline lives here when on paper.

moss.description: Section overlay tint (Agencies on the live site). Deep moss green.

forest-deep.description: Section overlay tint (Events on the live site). Deep forest green.

blue-muted.description: Pale blue-grey. Editorial accent. The cool counterweight to the olive primary.

blue-slate.description: Deeper blue-grey. Partner / dark-mode pair to blue-muted.

sage-light.description: Sage-grey. Lighter cousin of primary — softer, more atmospheric.

sage-mint.description: Pale sage-green. Category pill / soft tag.

mauve.description: Dusty mauve. Cool plum complement to the warm darks — fills an empty register in the wheel.

taupe.description: Warm mid-neutral between cream and muted-surface.

peach.description: Pale peach / blush. Distinct hue from cream — reads skin/figure rather than paper.

mocha.description: Warm mid-tone. Bridges cream and the dark backgrounds.

border.description: Heading delimiter / hairline stroke. Light grey.

muted-surface.description: Card / icon-tile background on dark surfaces.

surface-warm.description: Dark maroon hero canvas behind dimmed photo overlay. Warm dark.

white-surface.description: Lightest neutral. Card edges / dividers on light surfaces.

bg-light.description: Long-form body background (long-form mode). Use for workbooks, reports, print PDFs.

fg.description: Default foreground type on dark surfaces (marquee mode).

fg-on-light.description: Foreground type on light surfaces (long-form mode). Paper does double duty as ink-on-light because the v1.0 palette has no separate near-black token.

fg-muted.description: Secondary type / metadata on dark surfaces (marquee mode).

fg-muted-light.description: Secondary type / metadata on light surfaces (long-form mode). Resolves to taupe (#706250) — warm mid-neutral. For a cooler neutral on paper-light, use color.role.fg-muted-cool-light below.

fg-muted-cool-light.description: Cool grey-green muted type on paper-light. Use when taupe reads too warm — captions inside primary-tinted surfaces, footers next to olive marks. Added 1.6.0 in response to 2026-05-12 field-use report.

stroke.description: Default hairline / divider color (#DDDDDD — high-contrast on dark surfaces).

rule-on-paper.description: Subtle hairline / rule color on paper (dark) surfaces. Muted version of primary, ~60% opacity equivalent. Use for body-text rules, workbook answer lines, callout dividers — anywhere color.ui.border (#DDDDDD) reads too loud. Added 1.6.0.

rule-on-secondary.description: Rule color inside secondary (#4E5041) callouts. Lighter than secondary, dimmer than cream. Added 1.6.0.

bold-variant.note: Real Bold is opt-in via the .oddtoe-headline--bold class. Otto sources the Pro cut separately; until then, the bold variant falls back to the default 400 rendering.

headline.description: Bebas Neue. Used for the anchor headline. Tall, narrow, all-caps by design. Weight 400 (Regular) is the default everywhere — web, deck, Word, PDF, video. Synthetic 700 is no longer used (locked 1.6.0 — see 08_decisions/2026-05-12-bebas-default-weight-400.md) because rendering varied unreliably across Word, LibreOffice, and PDF viewers. Chicago-rule title case applied via authored markup: major words literal UPPERCASE, minor words literal lowercase. Never italicized.

leadin.description: Qwigley. Conversational script lead-in that sits ABOVE the headline. Sentence case, not Chicago. Markup level varies (H2 above H1, or H3 above H2) — the role is what matters, not the heading level. Renamed from 'Quigley' in 0.2.0 — the font on the live site is the free Google Fonts family 'Qwigley', not the Comicraft 'Quigley'.

subtitle.description: Arvo Bold, uniform weight across every word. Chicago-rule applies to CASE only (majors UPPERCASE, minors lowercase); weight is always 700. Sits below the Bebas headline. Example: 'ATTENTION-GRABBING creative for SCREENS'.

body.source: Google Fonts (free) — load all four cuts: Regular, Italic, Bold, Bold Italic.
body.description: Arvo Regular for body prose. Bold inline within body to highlight keyphrases. Italic and Bold Italic available for body emphasis and pull-quotes — never used in headlines.

mono.description: Code/data fallback — Otto to confirm or replace.

leadinToHeadline.description: How the Qwigley lead-in is sized relative to the Bebas headline it leads into. Ratio is tiered because a script with lowercase has lower x-height than a display caps face — at smaller headlines the ratio needs to be larger so the script doesn't feel dwarfed.

floor.description: Lower bound for the lead-in on very small viewports.

gapEm.description: Negative margin-top on the Bebas headline so it sits up into the Qwigley descender space. Scales with headline size because it's em-based.

lockupGaps.description: Vertical spacing inside the Oddtoe headline lockup. Order top→bottom: Qwigley lead-in → Bebas headline → divider → Arvo subtitle → first body block. Locked 2026-04-22 in v1.1.0 from the divider preview artifact (Otto's eye).

headlineToDivider.description: Bebas headline bottom to divider top. Tight enough to read as a single lockup, loose enough to give the divider its own moment.

dividerToSubtitle.description: Divider bottom to Arvo subtitle top. Slightly more than the gap above so the subtitle doesn't crowd the rule.

subtitleToBody.description: Arvo subtitle baseline area to the first body block. Just enough breath that the body reads as a separate paragraph, not as part of the lockup.

rule.description: Oddtoe leading rule for body and subheads: line-height = font-size + 4pt. Tight at display sizes, generous at body sizes.

headline.description: Bebas display headlines only — tight, no +4pt rule.

display-headline.description: Baseline tracking for Bebas 700 synthetic display. Locked 2026-04-21.

subtitle.description: Arvo subtitle tracking. Softened from 0.22em in 1.4.4 — the wider value read as monumental; 0.04em is a minor spread that still reads as typographic.

body.description: Body prose is always left-aligned inside its container. See layout.sideBySideProse for when long passages should be split.

lead-intro.description: Reserved for a single-sentence lead intro paragraph only — never multi-sentence prose.

titleRule.description: Capitalize first and last words and all major words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, subordinating conjunctions). Lowercase: articles (a, an, the), the seven coordinating conjunctions (and, but, for, nor, or, so, yet), prepositions of any length when used as prepositions (in, on, of, by, with, from, into, over, under, through, between, against, around, across, despite, during, within, without, throughout, etc.), and 'to' in infinitives.

headlineStyle.value: Chicago rule on CASE; weight is uniform 700 (synthetic) throughout.
headlineStyle.description: Bebas headline: majors in literal UPPERCASE, minors in literal lowercase, every letter at synthetic weight 700. The Chicago rule decides UPPER vs lower — it does NOT affect weight.

subtitleStyle.value: Chicago rule on CASE; weight is uniform 700 throughout.
subtitleStyle.description: Arvo subtitle beneath the Bebas headline. Same Chicago logic as the headline: majors UPPERCASE, minors lowercase, all 700. Example: 'ATTENTION-GRABBING creative for SCREENS'.

intro.description: Single-sentence lead intro under a headline + subtitle lock-up. Centered because it is short. Never used for multi-sentence prose.

prose.description: Default body copy. Left-aligned inside its container. 450px ≈ 53 characters per line at 16px Arvo — a tight editorial reading rhythm. Locked 2026-04-22 in v1.2.0; previously 680px (~80ch) which was wider than Otto's eye preferred.

sideBySideProse.rule: Two independent paragraph blocks placed side-by-side.
sideBySideProse.description: When a body passage runs long (~120+ words or 6+ sentences), split it into TWO independent paragraph blocks placed side-by-side — not a CSS multi-column container flowing one text across two columns. Each block is a self-contained thought, each block is left-aligned, the container may be centered on the page. Container/gap locked 2026-04-22 in v1.2.0 against the new 450px single-column rhythm: 840px container + 32px gap yields two ~404px columns (~48ch each), tighter than the single-column read on purpose.

media.description: System-wide corner radius for ALL image surfaces — carousel cells, card photos, image-array photos, hero images, thumbnails. Locked 2026-04-22 in v1.3.0 against the carousel-cell radius from oddtoe.com. Use radius.media on the image itself even when it sits inside a card with a different container radius (e.g. radius.lg = 16px). The card container can be 16px and the photo inside it 10px — the image-corner feel stays consistent across components.

organic.description: Topiary-inspired blobby radius for hero shapes

divider._basis: Hairline strokes used inside the headline lockup as a delimiter between the Bebas headline and the Arvo subtitle. Two variants ship as siblings — pick one per layout. Color resolves through color.role.stroke (= color.ui.border = #DDDDDD).

color.description: Both variants use the stroke role.

width.description: Short solid lockup divider — narrow, quiet.
Short dashed lockup divider — wider, more textured.

carousel._basis: General carousel pattern lifted from oddtoe.com. Slick Carousel under the hood on the live site. Three legal cell variants — pick one per carousel instance, do not mix.

autoplayMs.description: Slide-advance interval. Pause on hover honored.

infinite.description: Loop continuously rather than bounce at the ends.

centerMode.description: Active slide is visually emphasized in the centre of the visible row.

slidesToShow._basis: Cells visible at each breakpoint. 1 mobile / 3 small tablet / 4 large tablet / 5 desktop.

arrows.description: Custom prev/next buttons outside the Slick default markup. Circle, 1px stroke in color.role.fg-muted (cream), transparent fill.

counter.description: Two-digit current / total displayed below the row. Arvo, 11px, 0.18em tracking, cream.

dots.description: Pagination dots below the counter. 6px circles, cream at 35% inactive / 100% active.

cell._basis: All cells use radius.media (10px). Pick one variant per instance.

background.description: Logos sit on a warm off-white tile so the brand colour reads cleanly regardless of host surface.

logo.use: Client / partner logo strip. Up to 18 logos per instance is fine — the live site has 18 in one of its three carousels.

padding.description: Image fills the cell flush to radius.media.

image.use: Editorial photo / installation shot strip. Pair with a section heading above; do not put text inside the cell.

contentCard.use: Embeds an Image-first or Title-first work card as a carousel slide. Defer to cards.md for the cell's internal layout.

instancesPerPage.description: oddtoe.com runs three carousel instances on the home page. More than three on a single page is a smell — consider whether a static grid would serve better.

imageArray._basis: The 'Title-first' work tile pattern from oddtoe.com's 'Examples of Past... Creative Work in the Studio' section. Sizes are component-scoped — they are NOT new global type roles. Do not reuse these values outside the Image Array unless you've decided the type system needs a fifth role and updated typography.md.

size.description: Bebas headline at component scope. Smaller than any global headline tier — these tiles sit in a 4-up grid where each title is a label, not an anchor.

case.description: Same Chicago-rule treatment as the global headline.

size.description: Small label above the title (e.g. 'Documentaries · Melbourne'). Component-scoped — see _basis.

order.description: Title-first card order. The opposite ordering (image → title → location → description) lives under cards.md as the 'Image-first' variant.

shadow._basis: Cast using color.brand.paper (#262B2A) — the dark-first canonical body surface. Re-derive these rgba() literals if paper changes.

reduceMotion.value: honor prefers-reduced-motion: scale transitions to 0ms for non-essential motion

engine._basis: Canonical motion engines per surface. Locked 2026-04-22 in v1.4.0. The engine choice belongs in tokens (not just docs) so generated code reaches for the right library reference and so future audits can grep for engine drift. See 04_motion/motion-principles.md for the full rationale and 08_decisions/2026-04-22-motion-engine.md for the decision log.

web.license: Standard (free) — Webflow-sponsored since the 2025 free-license announcement following Webflow's fall 2024 acquisition of GreenSock. Includes all previously paid Club plugins (SplitText, MorphSVG, DrawSVG). One restriction: cannot be used to build a Webflow-competitor visual animation editor; not applicable to Datalabs / Oddtoe work.
web.use: All web and interactive motion (landing pages, micro-interactions, scroll-triggered reveals, parallax). Recipes that ship JS live in 04_motion/scroll-recipes.md and animation-recipes.md.

video.library: Adobe After Effects (master) → Lottie / Bodymovin (web export)
video.use: Long-form animated content — Oddtoe TV shorts, case-study videos, title-card sequences. Master in After Effects; export to Lottie JSON when the same animation also needs to play on the web at vector quality. The Lottie bridge is documented as an intent in v1.4.0 but is not yet wired into a working export — first real Oddtoe TV piece will lock that pipeline.

presentations.use: Decks. Map fade/slide tokens to native transition picks per 06_templates/presentation-theme.md. Do NOT embed video for transitional motion that a native transition can express — file size balloons and the transition reads as foreign.

social.use: Social-cut videos (Reels, TikTok, square feed). Same master pipeline as long-form video; renders to MP4 at the aspect ratios in video.aspectRatios.
